finding.CYCLE.detected.explanation: None of the components involved can be deployed, started or recovered on its own. If the cycle is synchronous, one of them going down blocks the rest.
finding.CYCLE.detected.suggestion: Break the cycle by inverting one of the dependencies, or replace it with asynchronous communication over a queue.
finding.CYCLE.passed.explanation: The dependencies between components were followed and none doubles back on itself: they can all be deployed and started in some order.
finding.EXPOSED_DATABASE.passed.explanat: Getting to the data means going through an API or a gateway first, which is where you can check who is calling.
finding.EXPOSED_DATABASE.reachable.expla: Outside traffic reaches the database directly, so there is nowhere to check who is calling or what they are asking for.
finding.EXPOSED_DATABASE.reachable.messa: '{node}' can be reached without going through any API.
finding.EXPOSED_DATABASE.reachable.sugge: Put an API or a gateway in front, and let only that talk to the database.
finding.HIGH_COUPLING.fanOut.explanation: A component that needs that many pieces to work is hard to deploy, test and reason about in isolation, and its availability is the product of all of theirs.
finding.HIGH_COUPLING.fanOut.suggestion: Check whether some of those responsibilities belong to the component itself, or whether part of the calls could become asynchronous events.
finding.HIGH_COUPLING.passed.explanation: How many components each one depends on was counted, and none needs so many pieces that it becomes hard to deploy or test on its own.
finding.HIGH_COUPLING.passed.message: No component piles up too many dependencies.
finding.MISSING_CACHE.direct.explanation: The whole read load falls on the same instance, which becomes the scaling limit of the entire system.

finding.MISSING_CACHE.direct.message.one: '{node}' takes direct queries from {count} component with no cache and no read replica.
finding.MISSING_CACHE.direct.message.other: '{node}' takes direct queries from {count} components with no cache and no read replica.

finding.MISSING_CACHE.direct.suggestion: Put a cache in front of the most frequent reads, or configure read replicas on the database.
finding.MISSING_CACHE.passed.explanation: Who queries each database was checked: none takes enough direct load to become the scaling limit of the system.
finding.MISSING_CACHE.passed.message: Database access is backed by a cache or by replicas.
finding.MISSING_RESILIENCE.exposedToSpof: Since '{target}' is a single point of failure, it going down propagates straight back up.
Add a circuit breaker or an alternative answer for when the destination does not reply.
finding.MISSING_RESILIENCE.noTimeout.exp: With no timeout, a slow answer holds on to resources indefinitely.
finding.MISSING_RESILIENCE.noTimeout.sug: Configure a timeout in line with the operation.
finding.MISSING_RESILIENCE.noTimeoutAndS: With no timeout, a slow answer holds on to resources indefinitely — and since '{target}' is a single point of failure, it going down propagates straight back up.
Configure a timeout in line with the operation, and add a circuit breaker or an alternative answer for when the destination does not reply.
finding.MISSING_RESILIENCE.passed.explan: Every synchronous call has a timeout bounding it and, where the destination is critical, an alternative to fall back on if it does not answer.
finding.MISSING_RESILIENCE.passed.messag: The synchronous calls are protected against failure.
finding.MISSING_RESILIENCE.unprotected.m: The call from '{source}' to '{target}' has no protection against failure.
finding.NO_OBSERVABILITY.explanation: When something fails there will be nowhere to look: not which component started it, not how long it was taking, not how many requests were lost. The failure gets investigated from memory.
finding.NO_OBSERVABILITY.orphan.message: The observability component is not connected to anything.
finding.NO_OBSERVABILITY.passed.explanat: There is an observability component wired up, so when something fails there will be somewhere to look.
finding.NO_OBSERVABILITY.suggestion: Add an observability component and wire up whatever you want to be able to look at when something goes wrong.
finding.NO_RATE_LIMIT.passed.explanation: The gateway turns away whatever goes over the limit at the door, instead of letting it pile up on what is behind it.
finding.NO_RATE_LIMIT.passed.message: The entry point caps how many requests it takes.
finding.NO_RATE_LIMIT.unlimited.explanat: Everything that arrives gets in, so a spike — or somebody pushing on purpose — propagates all the way inwards and the most fragile component pays for it.
finding.NO_RATE_LIMIT.unlimited.message: '{node}' does not limit the requests it accepts.
finding.NO_RATE_LIMIT.unlimited.suggesti: Set a request limit in line with what the components behind it can take: the excess is rejected at the door, which is where it is cheap.
finding.ORPHAN_NODE.disconnected.explana: It neither receives calls nor makes any, so it is not part of any flow in the architecture.
finding.ORPHAN_NODE.disconnected.suggest: Wire it to whatever should call it or whatever it should call, or delete it if it is left over.
finding.ORPHAN_NODE.passed.explanation: A component with no incoming and no outgoing calls takes part in no flow, so no other rule can say anything about it.
finding.ORPHAN_NODE.passed.message: Every component is connected to something.
finding.QUEUE_NO_DLQ.missing.explanation: A message that cannot be processed is retried, fails again and disappears without a trace. Nobody finds out what was lost.
finding.QUEUE_NO_DLQ.missing.suggestion: Turn on the dead letter queue so whatever fails ends up somewhere it can be reviewed.
finding.QUEUE_NO_DLQ.passed.explanation: A message that keeps failing ends up in the dead letter queue instead of being lost, and there it can be looked at.
finding.QUEUE_NO_DLQ.passed.message: The queues have somewhere to put what cannot be processed.
finding.RETRY_AMPLIFICATION.chain.messag: Retries multiply along the chain {walk}: up to {factor:number} requests for every original one.
finding.RETRY_AMPLIFICATION.explanation: When a service starts failing, the retries at each hop multiply with each other and add load precisely on the component that is already in trouble.
finding.RETRY_AMPLIFICATION.passed.expla: Retries were multiplied along every synchronous chain and none of them builds up into an avalanche of requests.
finding.RETRY_AMPLIFICATION.passed.messa: The retries that are configured do not amplify along a chain.
finding.RETRY_AMPLIFICATION.suggestion: Retry only at the hop closest to the failure, add growing waits between attempts, and cap retries on the stretches in between.

finding.RETRY_AMPLIFICATION.unbounded.me.one: The call from '{source}' to '{target}' retries {retries:number} time with no timeout to bound it.
finding.RETRY_AMPLIFICATION.unbounded.me.other: The call from '{source}' to '{target}' retries {retries:number} times with no timeout to bound them.

finding.SPOF.explanation: There is no equivalent component that could take over its work. Anything that happens to it affects everything behind it.
finding.SPOF.passed.explanation: Component by component, what would stop working if it went down was checked: none of them takes the rest of the system with it.
finding.SPOF.passed.message: No single component concentrates how the system works.

finding.SPOF.shared.message.one: '{node}' is a single point of failure: {count} component depends on it with no redundancy.
finding.SPOF.shared.message.other: '{node}' is a single point of failure: {count} components depend on it with no redundancy.

finding.SPOF.suggestion: Add a LoadBalancer with at least two equivalent instances, or replicate the component so its consumers have an alternative.

finding.SPOF.unreachable.message.one: '{node}' is a single point of failure: {count} component becomes unreachable if it stops working.
finding.SPOF.unreachable.message.other: '{node}' is a single point of failure: {count} components become unreachable if it stops working.

finding.SYNC_CHAIN.long.explanation: The request is not finished until the last link answers: the latencies add up, and one of them failing is enough for all of them to fail.

finding.SYNC_CHAIN.long.message.one: '{node}' starts a synchronous dependency chain of {count} component.
finding.SYNC_CHAIN.long.message.other: '{node}' starts a synchronous dependency chain of {count} components.

finding.SYNC_CHAIN.long.suggestion: Cut the chain by introducing a queue at the point where the operation stops needing an immediate answer.
finding.SYNC_CHAIN.passed.explanation: The synchronous calls were walked and none chains enough components for the latencies to add up.
finding.SYNC_CHAIN.passed.message: There are no long synchronous chains.
finding.TIMEOUT_TOO_SHORT.expires.explan: It costs {callMs:durationPrecise} with everything working and the timeout is {timeoutMs:durationPrecise}: it expires every time, so '{target}' behaves as if it were permanently down.
finding.TIMEOUT_TOO_SHORT.expires.messag: The timeout on the call from '{source}' to '{target}' is shorter than the call itself.
finding.TIMEOUT_TOO_SHORT.expires.sugges: Raise the timeout above {callMs:durationPrecise}, or shorten the call by removing hops along the way.
finding.TIMEOUT_TOO_SHORT.passed.explana: Every timeout is longer than what that call costs with everything working, so it only fires when something is genuinely wrong.
finding.TIMEOUT_TOO_SHORT.passed.message: The timeouts give the call time to finish.
finding.UNAUTHENTICATED_ENTRY.open.expla: It is a way in from outside and there is a database behind it, so anyone who knows the address reaches the data.
finding.UNAUTHENTICATED_ENTRY.open.sugge: Turn on authentication at the entry point, or put a gateway in front that does it.
finding.UNAUTHENTICATED_ENTRY.passed.exp: Anyone arriving from outside has to identify themselves before the request reaches anything that stores data.
finding.UNAUTHENTICATED_ENTRY.passed.mes: The front doors ask for authentication.
It receives {loadRps:number} rps and handles {capacityRps:number}, {utilization:percent} of its capacity. Any spike above what was declared knocks it over.
'{node}' is at the edge of its capacity.
It receives {loadRps:number} rps and handles {capacityRps:number}, {utilization:percent} of its capacity. What does not fit is rejected, and what does fit waits longer.
'{node}' takes more requests than it can handle.
finding.UNDERSIZED_COMPONENT.passed.expl: Every component takes what reaches it with room to spare, so a spike does not knock it over.
finding.UNDERSIZED_COMPONENT.passed.mess: No component is near its capacity under the declared load.
Put a cache in front so not everything reaches it, add read replicas, or move the work that can wait out of the request.
Add consumers: the queue copes, what cannot keep up is whoever drains it.
Give it more instances, or split its work across several components.
fix.MISSING_CACHE.insert: Put a cache in front of '{node}'
fix.MISSING_RESILIENCE.timeoutAndFallbac: Set a {seconds:number} s timeout and an alternative answer
fix.QUEUE_NO_DLQ.enable: Turn on the dead letter queue
metric.backlogRps: Work piling up in the queues
sim.edge.contained: '{target}' does not answer and the alternative replies.
sim.edge.injected: A fault was injected into this call: the destination is still alive, but it cannot be reached.
sim.edge.instanceDown: The instance it routes to is not answering.
sim.edge.noTimeout: '{target}' does not answer and the call has no timeout: it waits {waitMs:duration} without giving up.
sim.edge.timeoutExceeded: It takes {callMs:duration} against a {timeoutMs:duration} timeout: it expires every time.
sim.edge.unprotected: '{target}' does not answer and the call has no alternative.
sim.edge.unreachable: It never happens: whoever originates it gets no traffic from '{cause}'.
sim.node.contained: '{target}' does not answer, but the alternative answer keeps the service up. It still works, with less.
sim.node.degradedDependency: '{target}' answers worse, and its call drags the degradation along.
sim.node.injected: A fault was injected into this component.
sim.node.instanceDown.contained: One of its instances is not answering; the health check routes traffic to the rest.
sim.node.instanceDown.spreading: One of its instances is not answering and it still receives traffic: with no health check, the degradation does not stop here.
sim.node.noTimeout: Its call to '{target}' has no timeout: it waits indefinitely, and neither the retry nor the fallback get to run.
sim.node.noWork: No work reaches it because the queue is unavailable.
sim.node.overloaded: It receives {loadRps:number} rps and handles {capacityRps:number}: it serves {served:number} out of every 100 requests and rejects the rest.
sim.node.queueDown: The work is not enqueued, but it keeps serving requests.
sim.node.saturated: It is at {utilization:percent} of its capacity: it receives {loadRps:number} rps and handles {capacityRps:number}. Any spike knocks it over.
sim.node.timeoutExceeded: The call to '{target}' takes {callMs:duration} and the timeout is {timeoutMs:duration}: it expires every time, as if '{target}' were down.
sim.node.unprotected: Its call to '{target}' has no alternative when '{target}' does not answer.
sim.node.unreachable: No traffic reaches it: '{cause}' was its way in.
